page: The Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a dedicated bare metal instance provisioned with an Intel Xeon E-2288G processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The server includes 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads operating at a base clock frequency of 3.7 GHz. Memory is configured with 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU thread. The machine is bundled with 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. It contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show dependable middle-tier compute throughput across general multi-core and single-core suites. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 18,785.52, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,690.0, and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 19,837.37. Single-threaded data compression represents a distinct strength, with gzip compression reaching 36.22 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 14.23 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25%. In memory tests, it achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,594.89, though sustained large-block uncached read and write bandwidths were limited to 29.76 GB/sec and 15.32 GB/sec respectively.

Hardware tradeoffs are evident in vector computation and AI workloads. While the Xeon E-2288G supports AVX, AES, and FMA instructions, it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Consequently, large language model generation using a medium 7B model drops to 7.56 tokens per second, landing in the bottom quartile. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform delivers strong non-virtualized single-tenant execution, dense local NVMe storage, and a high memory-to-core allocation without the virtualization overhead typically found in standard multi-tenant cloud instances.

The hardware configuration suits dedicated relational database instances, memory-intensive caching clusters such as Redis, continuous integration build servers, and static web serving nodes that capitalize on the combined 128 GB memory space and high-speed local NVMe subsystem.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a dedicated bare metal server powered by an Intel Xeon E-2288G processor offering 8 physical cores and 16 threads at 3.7 GHz. It includes 128.0 GB of DDR4-3000 memory and 3840 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage, operating without hypervisor overhead or discrete GPUs. CPU benchmarks reflect solid midrange capability with an 18,785.52 PassMark CPU score and 8,690.0 in Geekbench multi-core, complemented by top-tier single-threaded compression performance. While large-block memory throughput and vector-heavy workloads like 7B LLM inference show limitations due to the lack of AVX-512 extensions, the instance provides high memory capacity per core alongside massive local fast storage. This architecture is well suited for dedicated database hosting, large caching nodes, software compilation pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving.
